summary: Careful, well‑documented preregistered paired study with strong artifact hygiene, but the experimental design and reporting leave a critical ambiguity that makes the main confirmatory claim uninformative. The paper observes zero failures in both arms, yet does not convincingly demonstrate that the Guarded pipeline was given opportunity to differ from Baseline (shared_initial generation + no reported validator rejections or repair attempts). Key statistical result is therefore a null outcome driven by a ceiling/floor effect and/or by a design choice that collapses the two conditions; substantive clarifications, additional analyses or an amended experiment are required before acceptance.
critical_issues: Preregistered design used a single shared initial candidate per task across conditions (independent_condition_generation=false / generation_semantics="shared_initial_candidate"), yet the manuscript treats Baseline vs Guarded as a substantive intervention — this choice collapses the intervention unless the validator/repair path actually modified outputs. The paper fails to report basic counts showing that Guarded ever differed from Baseline (validator rejects, deterministic repair calls, repaired outputs).

All 400 paired outcomes are n11 (success in both conditions) with zero discordant pairs; the confirmatory statistical test and CI are therefore degenerate and uninformative about validator efficacy. The manuscript does not demonstrate that the study could have detected a nontrivial effect given the chosen generation semantics and observed validator behavior.

Reporting omission: no summary counts or summary examples are given for (a) validator acceptance/rejection decisions, (b) number of repair attempts invoked and their results, and (c) whether/when the Guarded condition applied a repaired configuration instead of the shared candidate. These are essential to interpret the null result.

Potential scoring/validator correctness issue not investigated: with zero failures observed, the manuscript must show that the scoring/operational failure detector (emulator checks, reachability/policy validation) had appropriate sensitivity (e.g., positive controls, injected failing tasks) rather than producing false negatives. No such sanity checks or negative controls are reported.

Preregistration vs execution tension: preregistered hypotheses assumed baseline failure ≥20% and a ≥40% relative reduction; the study outcome strongly departs from these assumptions. The manuscript does not show preplanned contingency plans or stopping‑rule diagnostics that explain the mismatch and its implications for interpretability.

Limited external validity acknowledged but underspecified: single model (gpt‑5‑mini), single adapter, shared initial generation, public/synthetic intents, and emulator fidelity together make the null result a weak basis for operational claims — the paper must make those limits explicit in the main claims and tone down broad conclusions.
required_revisions: Explicitly report validator and repair activity aggregated across the 400 tasks: validator pass rate, validator reject count, number of repair calls invoked, number of repairs that changed the candidate, and per‑condition final applied‑configuration counts with pointers to representative artifacts. If validator/repair counts are zero, state that clearly and discuss implications for the comparison.

Explain and justify the preregistered choice to use a shared initial candidate across conditions (independent_condition_generation=false / generation_semantics="shared_initial_candidate"). Document in the manuscript how and when the Guarded condition could have differed from Baseline under that design and why that design was selected. Discuss how this choice affects interpretability of H1–H2.

Provide evidence that the operational failure detector and scoring pipeline were capable of detecting real failures (negative/positive controls). If no positive controls were run, add an explicit limitation and, if possible, run and report a small set of injected failing tasks or synthetic negatives to demonstrate scorer sensitivity.

Reframe the main claims and abstract to accurately reflect that (a) the study observed no failures, and (b) the absence of observed failures may be caused by task difficulty, shared generation semantics, validator behavior, or emulator leniency rather than by intrinsic model safety. Remove or soften any wording that implies general safety or meaningful validator benefit beyond the constrained experimental boundary.

Add a short table (or text summary) characterizing the 400 intents (change types, vendor emulated, difficulty proxies) and include 3–5 concrete example intent→CLI artifacts (with file pointers/hashes) so readers can assess task difficulty and generalizability.

If feasible within review time, run and report one of the following: (A) rerun a randomized subset (e.g., 100 tasks) with independent per‑condition generation (initial_generation_calls_per_task=2 / independent_condition_generation=true) so that Baseline and Guarded start from different candidates, or (B) rerun a subset with adversarial/harder intents expected to cause failures (to demonstrate validator effect and scorer sensitivity). At minimum, explain why such reruns were not feasible and how future work will address them.
optional_revisions: Expand methodology discussion of the decision to limit repairs to a single deterministic LLM call and whether repair prompts/settings or validator rule coverage were tuned; include validator rule examples or pseudocode in an appendix or artifact pointer.

Provide a concise per‑task audit sample (e.g., 10 tasks) showing the initial candidate, validator verdict, any repair output, and emulator scoring timeline to help readers follow the pipeline end‑to‑end.

Add more explicit discussion and quantification of power/sensitivity under the actual observed outcomes (i.e., show that given zero discordant pairs, the study cannot bound meaningful reductions), and include suggested minimal detectable effects for alternative designs (independent generation, adversarial inputs).

Clarify in the Disclosure Statement the exact location (file path or persistent archive) of the preserved master prompt text and of the validator implementation code so reviewers can directly inspect them.
